_readme: One reward track per character: the hundred-level rail on the reward-track screen, levels 2-100 (RewardTrack.StartingLevel/MaxLevel; level 1 is where a character starts, not somewhere they arrive). A track is described, not levelled -- an author writes twelve milestones and a filler mix, and the game computes where every filler node lands. EVERY TRACK SHARES THE SAME TWELVE MILESTONE LEVELS -- 10, 20, 25, 30, 40, 45, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100 -- because the screen bakes milestone-ness (disc size, ring sprite, caption font) into the built scene at build time; only the CONTENT at each level is per-character. The remaining 87 levels are FILLER, authored as a MIX of (reward, amount, count) rows rather than as levels: 'count' is how many of the 87 filler levels that row occupies, and 'amount' is what it pays each time. A character with no entry in 'tracks' gets RewardTrackDefinition.Default instead -- the spine (Respec at 20, ten stat points at 80, a second life at 90) plus MaxHealth at the other nine milestones and a StatPoint/MaxHealth filler mix, so an undesigned character still shows a plain, honest track rather than a blank or broken one. The five validation rules RewardTrackEntryResolver enforces: (1) every one of the twelve milestone levels carries exactly one entry, and no entry names a level that is not one of the twelve, AND a one-shot capability -- Respec, SecondLife, SignatureAbsorbs, UnlockSkill -- may appear at most once across the milestones (UnlockSkill is keyed by its own skillId, so two milestones naming two different skills both count, but the same skill named twice does not), because HasUnlocked only ever asks whether the FIRST level a capability appears at has been reached, so a second copy would be content no player could ever see paid out; (2) the filler counts in one track's 'filler' array sum to exactly 87; (3) a one-shot capability -- the same four rule 1 names -- may only be a milestone, never filler, because filler's placement is computed and always starts at level 2, before an author could deliberately delay it; (4) a FILLER ElementalDamagePercent entry's 'against' must be an element the character can already deal at level 1 (their own attackType, a damageInstances type on a skill authored to them with unlockLevel <= 1, or an element a level-1 skill's own Elements list lets them choose -- an element the player can pick on demand counts the same as one the packet always deals) -- a milestone is exempt, since its level is authored and visible, so a milestone element can be placed deliberately after the skill that first deals it; (5) a signature reward (SignatureCapacity/GainPerTurn/GainOnDamageTaken/Absorbs) is refused on a character with no signatureId, because BuildSignatureResource would have nothing to pay it into. WHERE A FILLER NODE LANDS: the mix's declaration order does not matter, but the counts do -- InterleaveMix picks, at each of the 87 free levels in order starting from level 2, whichever row is furthest behind the share its count entitles it to (ties go to declaration order), so the row with the biggest count always takes level 2 and every row repeats at roughly its own even cadence across the whole track. reward is a TrackReward enum member name, matched case-insensitively; against is a DamageType name (Ice, not the skill-JSON-only alias Frost), read only by ElementalDamagePercent; skillId is read only by UnlockSkill and must name a real skill id -- the track's skill branch carries no ownership test, so a track may grant a skill authored to a different character (docs/PLAN_REWARD_TRACKS.md §3f/§3h). Field-by-field documentation, defaults and valid enum values: docs/CONTENT_SCHEMA.md. Design rationale for sheep's and owl's tracks: docs/PLAN_REWARD_TRACKS.md §5 — which predates bear's, authored 2026-09-11 on the owner's answer to AUDIT #134 and carrying its own _comment explaining what it could not mirror and why every number in it is a first value. Every character on the roster now has a track, so RewardTrackDefinition.Default is currently reached only by an id no row names; it is still the rule, not scaffolding.

milestones._comment: PLACEHOLDER, 2026-09-15: static_fleece was removed (AUDIT #150); this milestone needs a real replacement from the owner. StatPoint 2 keeps the track valid (every milestone level requires exactly one entry) without committing to a new unlock.

tracks._comment: FIRST VALUES, NOT BALANCED NUMBERS. Bjorn had no track at all until AUDIT #134 was answered with 'why not?', so until now he levelled 2-100 on RewardTrackDefinition.Default. The STRUCTURE here mirrors sheep's and owl's exactly -- the same twelve fixed milestone levels, filler summing to 87, Respec at 20 and SecondLife at 90 once each. WHAT COULD NOT BE MIRRORED, and why: (a) no Signature* reward, because Bjorn has no signatureId at all (rule 5 refuses one) -- his resource is the fury POOL, and TrackReward has nothing that pays into a primary pool other than mana, which is the model gap AUDIT #134 keeps open after this authoring; (b) no MaxMana and no ManaRegen, because fury's capacityRule is Fixed and restoredByManaEffects is false, so both would resolve clean and then pay nothing (blind spot B9); (c) no UnlockSkill milestone, because all three of his skills (placeholder_brawler_slam/_provoke/_ward) author unlockLevel 1 and are his from the start -- there is no skill left for a level to hand him, and a track may not grant the same skill twice. THE NUMBERS. StatPoint (10 at the level-80 spine, 1 x 40 filler = 50 total) and SecondLife 1 are copied straight off sheep. The three ElementalDamagePercent milestones copy sheep's own level-45 amount of 10 and name Physical, which is Bjorn's attackType and the type his level-1 slam therefore deals. The MaxHealth amounts are NOT copied off sheep: sheep's amounts in those slots are wool -- capacity and per-turn income -- and mean nothing as health. They come from RewardTrackDefinition.Default instead (15 a milestone), which is the track Bjorn is on today, so moving him onto this one pays roughly what he already had: 225 max health fully collected against the default's 229. All of it awaits the balance pass that also authors what Fury BUYS (see pools.json's fury _comment) -- treat every number here as a placeholder that resolves, not as a tuned one.
